title: Reliable AI-Assisted Decisions via Selective Auditing
abstract: arXiv:2610.31662v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: We consider online monitoring of an AI system that produces a sequence of decisions. At each round, the system outputs a proposed decision together with a confidence score estimating the trustworthiness of the decision. The decision and confidence score need not be produced by the same model: for example, one agent may propose a decision, while a separate verifier agent evaluates it and outputs a correctness or safety score. Based on this information, we must decide whether to accept the AI decision automatically or consult an expert, such as a human auditor, who reviews the proposal and either accepts or corrects it. We formulate this task as an online constrained optimization problem in which the goal is to minimize the frequency of expert auditing while guaranteeing that the fraction of AI errors that go unaudited stays below a user-defined threshold. translated_abstract: 我们考虑对产生一系列决策的AI系统进行在线监控。在每一轮中，系统输出一个提议的决策以及一个用于估计该决策可信度的置信分数。决策和置信分数不必由同一个模型产生：例如，一个智能体可能提出决策，而另一个独立的验证智能体对其进行评估并输出正确性或安全性分数。基于这些信息，我们必须决定是自动接受AI决策，还是咨询专家（例如人类审计员），由其审查该提案并接受或纠正它。我们将此任务表述为一个在线约束优化问题，其目标是最小化专家审计的频率，同时保证未经审计的AI错误比例保持在用户定义的阈值以下。我们推导出一族具有可证明错误控制保证的算法，无需（摘要在此处被截断）
tldr: 提出了一个在线选择性审计框架，在最小化专家审计频率的同时，提供可证明的错误控制保证，使未经审计的AI错误比例始终低于用户设定的阈值。
en_tdlr: This paper formulates selective auditing as an online constrained optimization problem and derives a family of algorithms with provable error-control guarantees that minimize expert auditing frequency while keeping the fraction of unaudited AI errors below a user-defined threshold.
